ca_main_cliff_band.blurb: Main Cliff Band is a bouldering wall inside Glen Canyon, a city park in San Francisco. It holds nine problems, all between V0 and V3: three at V0, three at V1, two at V2 and a single V3. Many follow cracks, ledgy faces and jug lines. The cliff reaches about 30 feet at its highest point, so the taller lines are highball territory and a spotter or extra pads are worth having. Climbing here goes back many decades, and the style suits a short session of moderate problems in the middle of town.

ca_emperor_boulder.blurb: Emperor Boulder is a large, rounded block roughly 60 to 70 feet tall, standing at the water's edge beside the Pacific at Mickey's Beach in Marin County. Despite the name, it is a sport climbing wall with nine bolted routes. They run from 5.11 to 5.13: two at 5.11, four at 5.12 and three at 5.13, so it suits strong climbers rather than newcomers. The rock is recently developed and still shedding flakes, so some holds feel loose until the lines clean up with traffic. Much of the beach climbing depends on the tide, so check the tables before you plan a day.

ca_the_black_manta_boulder.blurb: The Black Manta Boulder is one of five tightly grouped boulders at the core of Central Atlantis, part of the Tramway bouldering in the San Jacinto Mountains of California. It has nine problems and leans hard: one V0, then a run of problems from V5 up to V9, including a few harder variations and open projects. Sun and tree shade shift across its faces through the day, which helps when picking a time to try the steeper lines.

ca_quality_cliff.blurb: Quality Cliff is a steep, older-style sport crag above Fish Creek in the Rodeo Flat area of the Kern Plateau, at about 7,200 feet. It has nine routes, eight of them sport and one trad, ranging from 5.10 to 5.12 with most at 5.11. The lines were put up around 1990 and are steep and demanding, with lichen on the holds and some falls that run long, so a stick clip is handy. Bolts and anchors are aged, so inspect them before trusting them. It sits in the Fish Creek gorge alongside two other crags.

ca_the_solar_panel.blurb: The Solar Panel is a west-facing granodiorite wall in the Daff Area beside Tioga Road in Yosemite's Tuolumne region, at roughly 8,200 feet. It has nine routes, eight trad leads and one top-rope, all between 5.7 and 5.9, with most at 5.8 or 5.9. Because it takes a lot of sun, the base tends to be warm and dry early in the season while other crags still hold snow; hot midsummer days are less comfortable, and late season suits it well. Reaching it takes a walk of about a mile and a half return along the creek trail, then a short scramble up ramps to two terraces.

ca_quaking_aspen_wall.blurb: Quaking Aspen Wall is a granite wall on the Tioga Cliff in Lee Vining Canyon, in the Eastern Sierra at about 9,000 feet. It forms the bottom step of the main Tioga cliff line, and an aspen grove frames its left side. Nine routes, seven sport and two trad, climb mostly vertical, featured rock. Grades start at 5.9 and top out in the 5.11 range, with most routes at 5.10 and 5.11, so it works for a climber stepping up to the lower double digits. The walk in from the right end of the Tioga Wall is short.

ca_quarter_day_dome.blurb: Quarter Day Dome is a granodiorite dome on Shuteye Ridge, in the Southern Sierra west of the crest and reached from the Chilkoot Lake side near Highway 41, at about 7,700 feet. It is divided into a lower and an upper section. All routes are single pitch, nearly all with chains for the rappel down. Nine routes, five trad and four sport, run from 5.7 up to 5.11, with the bulk around 5.9. Many trails and cross-country lines meet near the base, so a GPS track is useful for finding it.
